title: VECS database update – Manual fix
description: Certificate-manager had updated filesystem files but failed to update VECS (VMware Endpoint Certificate Store). vCenter reads certs from VECS on startup, not filesystem. Manual VECS update was required to complete certificate replacement.
close_reason: VECS updated successfully. Certificate now serving correctly.

comments.author: Claude Haiku 4.5
comments.text: Diagnosis: Previous agent session updated filesystem files (/etc/vmware-vpx/ssl/rui.crt and rui.key) with new certificate but VECS still contained the OLD certificate (notBefore=Feb 1 06:20:50 vs new cert notBefore=Feb 1 08:06:30). This mismatch meant vCenter services were still serving the old cert.

comments.author: Claude Haiku 4.5
comments.text:
Fix applied:
1. Deleted old VECS entry: vecs-cli entry delete --store MACHINE_SSL_CERT --alias __MACHINE_CERT -y
2. Created new VECS entry from filesystem: vecs-cli entry create --store MACHINE_SSL_CERT --alias __MACHINE_CERT --cert /etc/vmware-vpx/ssl/rui.crt --key /etc/vmware-vpx/ssl/rui.key
3. Restarted rhttpproxy only: service-control --stop vmware-rhttpproxy && service-control --start vmware-rhttpproxy

This minimal restart avoids the risky full service restart that certificate-manager attempts.
